messages.content:
The numbers 1, 2, ..., 2100 are written on a board. Every second, Mark takes two numbers on the board, \( a \) and \( b \), erases them, and replaces them with \( \gcd(a, b) \) and \( \operatorname{lcm}(a, b) \). Mark stops once any move he makes will not change the numbers written on the board. Compute the number of divisors of the 2026th smallest positive integer written on the board when he finishes.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
Looking at this problem, I need to understand what happens when Mark repeatedly replaces pairs $(a,b)$ with $(\gcd(a,b), \text{lcm}(a,b))$.

## Key Invariant

For each prime $p$, the **multiset of exponents** $\{v_p(n_1), v_p(n_2), \ldots, v_p(n_{2100})\}$ is preserved, since replacing exponents $e_1, e_2$ with $\min(e_1,e_2)$ and $\max(e_1,e_2)$ keeps the multiset unchanged.

## Final Configuration

Mark stops when every pair on the board satisfies $a \mid b$ (one divides the other), meaning the numbers form a **chain under divisibility**: $n_1 \mid n_2 \mid \cdots \mid n_{2100}$.

Since the exponents for each prime get "sorted" through the operations, the final state has:
$$n_k = \prod_p p^{e_{p,k}}$$
where $e_{p,1} \leq e_{p,2} \leq \cdots \leq e_{p,2100}$ are the sorted values of $\{v_p(1), v_p(2), \ldots, v_p(2100)\}$.

## Finding $e_{p,2026}$

The number of integers in $\{1,\ldots,2100\}$ with $v_p(j) = 0$ is $2100 - \lfloor 2100/p\rfloor$, with $v_p(j) \leq i$ is $2100 - \lfloor 2100/p^{i+1}\rfloor$.

So $e_{p,2026} \geq j$ iff $\lfloor 2100/p^j \rfloor \geq 75$ (since $2100 - 2026 = 74$).

Checking each prime:

| Prime $p$ | $\lfloor 2100/p\rfloor$ | $\lfloor 2100/p^2\rfloor$ | $\lfloor 2100/p^3\rfloor$ | $\lfloor 2100/p^4\rfloor$ | $e_{p,2026}$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 1050 ✓ | 525 ✓ | 262 ✓ | 131 ✓ | 4 |
| 3 | 700 ✓ | 233 ✓ | 77 ✓ | 25 ✗ | 3 |
| 5 | 420 ✓ | 84 ✓ | 16 ✗ | — | 2 |
| 7 | 300 ✓ | 42 ✗ | — | — | 1 |
| 11 | 190 ✓ | 17 ✗ | — | — | 1 |
| 13 | 161 ✓ | 12 ✗ | — | — | 1 |
| 17 | 123 ✓ | 7 ✗ | — | — | 1 |
| 19 | 110 ✓ | 5 ✗ | — | — | 1 |
| 23 | 91 ✓ | 3 ✗ | — | — | 1 |
| 29 | 72 ✗ | — | — | — | 0 |

## Computing the Answer

$$n_{2026} = 2^4 \cdot 3^3 \cdot 5^2 \cdot 7^1 \cdot 11^1 \cdot 13^1 \cdot 17^1 \cdot 19^1 \cdot 23^1$$

The number of divisors is:
$$(4+1)(3+1)(2+1)(1+1)^6 = 5 \cdot 4 \cdot 3 \cdot 2^6 = 60 \cdot 64 = 3840$$

$$\boxed{3840}$$
